L66@P4: Preface to the first edition.
L67@P4: In the late fifties and early sixties, Tate (and Poitou) found some important duality theorems concerning the Galois cohomology of finite modules and abelian
L68@P4: varieties over local and global fields.
L69@P4: About 1964, Artin and Verdier extended some of the results to ´etale cohomology groups over rings of integers in local and global fields.
L70@P4: Since then many people (Artin, Bester, B´egueri, Mazur, McCallum, the author, Roberts, Shatz, Vvedens’kii) have generalized these results to flat cohomology groups.
L71@P4: Much of the best of this work has not been fully published. My initial purpose
L72@P4: in preparing these notes was simply to write down a complete set of proofs before
L73@P4: they were forgotten, but I have also tried to give an organized account of the
L74@P4: whole subject. Only a few of the theorems in these notes are new, but many
L75@P4: results have been sharpened, and a significant proportion of the proofs have not
L76@P4: been published before.

L20@P1: — pureté, morphisme de Gysin et comparaison à la complet ion —, on utilise une
L21@P1: construction dont le principe est dû à Nagata : utilisant des « dilatations formelles »,
L22@P1: on construit un schéma noethérien strictement hensélien X de dimension 2, de complété X régulier de dimension 2, et une courbe irréductible C dans X devenant le
L23@P1: £-ième multiple d'un diviseur régulier dans X. Cette construction est ensuite étendue
L24@P1: au cas, plus délicat, de la dimension supérieure. À partir de là, on construit aisément

L29@P1: affine) du spectre épointé d'un schéma noethérien intègre strictement local.
